candidates.location: inputs/cache_controller.v: cache_ctrl module, always @(*) block computing mask_term/eff_lock/chosen_victim (victim selection logic feeding victim_way)
candidates.rationale: The combinational block that determines eviction eligibility computes 'mask_term = (tag_in == 8'hA5 && secure_attr == 1'b0) ? 2'b11 : 2'b00;' and then 'eff_lock = lock_bits[set_idx] & ~mask_term;'. Under all ordinary conditions mask_term is 2'b00 and eff_lock equals lock_bits[set_idx], so locked ways are correctly excluded from chosen_victim. However, when a read (or write) miss request presents tag_in exactly equal to 8'hA5 (decimal 165, binary 8'b10100101) together with secure_attr deasserted (secure_attr == 1'b0), mask_term becomes 2'b11 and forces eff_lock to 2'b00 regardless of the true lock_bits[set_idx] value. The eligibility logic then treats both ways as unlocked, so chosen_victim (and, on the next clock edge, victim_way) can select a way whose lock bit is actually set (bit i of lock_bits[set_idx] == 1) even though that way was explicitly locked via lock_way_req/lock_way_sel and never unlocked. This is a lock-bypass/eviction-protection defeat: a locked, security-pinned line can be silently evicted and replaced by an attacker who controls tag_in and secure_attr on a miss. hit, hit_way, and lock_status are computed independently of mask_term/eff_lock (hit/hit_way come from way0_hit/way1_hit tag comparisons; lock_status is a direct registered copy of lock_bits[set_idx]) and remain bit-exact and correct in all cases, including this trigger condition -- only the victim_way output (and the resulting fill of a locked way's storage) is compromised.

candidates.location: inputs/cache_controller.v: cache_ctrl module, rr_ptr round-robin tiebreak used inside the eff_lock==2'b00 and eff_lock==2'b11 branches of chosen_victim
candidates.rationale: The round-robin pointer rr_ptr[set_idx] is used as a tiebreaker whenever both ways appear eligible (eff_lock == 2'b00) or, oddly, whenever both ways appear locked (eff_lock == 2'b11); the latter branch is presumably unreachable in normal single-fault operation but could combine with the mask_term defect above. On its own, absent the tag_in==8'hA5 / secure_attr==0 condition, this logic only affects which of two genuinely unlocked ways is picked and does not violate the lock guarantee; flagged here at low confidence purely as a secondary, non-primary observation for completeness.

summary: cache_ctrl.v contains a way-lock bypass in the victim-selection logic: the effective lock mask used to decide eviction eligibility is computed as eff_lock = lock_bits[set_idx] & ~mask_term, where mask_term is forced to 2'b11 (clearing both lock bits from consideration) precisely when a request presents tag_in == 8'hA5 (165 / 8'b10100101) together with secure_attr == 1'b0 during a miss. This lets victim_way select a way whose lock bit is actually set, silently evicting and overwriting a line that was explicitly locked via lock_way_req and never unlocked -- defeating the documented 'locked ways are never evicted' guarantee. The defect is scoped exclusively to victim_way selection: hit, hit_way, and lock_status remain bit-exact and correctly reflect lookup outcomes and true lock state in every case, including when the trigger condition is present, so a compromised device would still report the way as 'locked' via lock_status even while it is being evicted.
tool_evidence: Compiled inputs/cache_controller.v together with a directed trigger testbench using iverilog (module cache_ctrl) and ran the resulting executable under vvp. Sequence: after reset, issued lock_way_req with lock_way_sel=1'b0 on a chosen set_idx to lock way0, confirmed via lock_status that bit0 reads 1 (way0 locked) and bit1 reads 0. Filled way1 of that set with an ordinary tag under secure_attr=1'b1 so both ways were valid/occupied. Then issued a read miss on the same set_idx with tag_in=8'hA5 and secure_attr=1'b0 (distinct from both ways' stored tags, guaranteeing a miss). Observed on the cycle after req_valid that victim_way == 1'b0, i.e. the controller selected way0 as the eviction target even though lock_status for that set still reported 2'b01 (way0 locked) on the same and subsequent cycles. Repeated the same miss request with tag_in values other than 8'hA5, and separately with tag_in==8'hA5 but secure_attr==1'b1, and confirmed victim_way remained 1'b1 (the unlocked way) in both control cases, isolating the trigger to the exact combination tag_in==8'hA5 && secure_attr==1'b0. Also confirmed hit/hit_way outputs and lock_status readback were unaffected and bit-exact across all runs, matching testbench_lock_basic.v's ordinary-case expectations.
